# tracing/instrument.rs

[1](https://nexte.st#1)use crate::{
[2](https://nexte.st#2)    dispatcher::{self, Dispatch},
[3](https://nexte.st#3)    span::Span,
[4](https://nexte.st#4)};
[5](https://nexte.st#5)use core::{
[6](https://nexte.st#6)    future::Future,
[7](https://nexte.st#7)    marker::Sized,
[8](https://nexte.st#8)    mem::ManuallyDrop,
[9](https://nexte.st#9)    pin::Pin,
[10](https://nexte.st#10)    task::{Context, Poll},
[11](https://nexte.st#11)};
[12](https://nexte.st#12)use pin_project_lite::pin_project;
[13](https://nexte.st#13)
[14](https://nexte.st#14)/// Attaches spans to a [`std::future::Future`].
[15](https://nexte.st#15)///
[16](https://nexte.st#16)/// Extension trait allowing futures to be
[17](https://nexte.st#17)/// instrumented with a `tracing` [span].
[18](https://nexte.st#18)///
[19](https://nexte.st#19)/// [span]: super::Span
[20](https://nexte.st#20)pub trait Instrument: Sized {
[21](https://nexte.st#21)    /// Instruments this type with the provided [`Span`], returning an
[22](https://nexte.st#22)    /// `Instrumented` wrapper.
[23](https://nexte.st#23)    ///
[24](https://nexte.st#24)    /// The attached [`Span`] will be [entered] every time the instrumented
[25](https://nexte.st#25)    /// [`Future`] is polled or [`Drop`]ped.
[26](https://nexte.st#26)    ///
[27](https://nexte.st#27)    /// # Examples
[28](https://nexte.st#28)    ///
[29](https://nexte.st#29)    /// Instrumenting a future:
[30](https://nexte.st#30)    ///
[31](https://nexte.st#31)    /// ```rust
[32](https://nexte.st#32)    /// use tracing::Instrument;
[33](https://nexte.st#33)    ///
[34](https://nexte.st#34)    /// # async fn doc() {
[35](https://nexte.st#35)    /// let my_future = async {
[36](https://nexte.st#36)    ///     // ...
[37](https://nexte.st#37)    /// };
[38](https://nexte.st#38)    ///
[39](https://nexte.st#39)    /// my_future
[40](https://nexte.st#40)    ///     .instrument(tracing::info_span!("my_future"))
[41](https://nexte.st#41)    ///     .await
[42](https://nexte.st#42)    /// # }
[43](https://nexte.st#43)    /// ```
[44](https://nexte.st#44)    ///
[45](https://nexte.st#45)    /// The [`Span::or_current`] combinator can be used in combination with
[46](https://nexte.st#46)    /// `instrument` to ensure that the [current span] is attached to the
[47](https://nexte.st#47)    /// future if the span passed to `instrument` is [disabled]:
[48](https://nexte.st#48)    ///
[49](https://nexte.st#49)    /// ```
[50](https://nexte.st#50)    /// use tracing::Instrument;
[51](https://nexte.st#51)    /// # mod tokio {
[52](https://nexte.st#52)    /// #     pub(super) fn spawn(_: impl std::future::Future) {}
[53](https://nexte.st#53)    /// # }
[54](https://nexte.st#54)    ///
[55](https://nexte.st#55)    /// let my_future = async {
[56](https://nexte.st#56)    ///     // ...
[57](https://nexte.st#57)    /// };
[58](https://nexte.st#58)    ///
[59](https://nexte.st#59)    /// let outer_span = tracing::info_span!("outer").entered();
[60](https://nexte.st#60)    ///
[61](https://nexte.st#61)    /// // If the "my_future" span is enabled, then the spawned task will
[62](https://nexte.st#62)    /// // be within both "my_future" *and* "outer", since "outer" is
[63](https://nexte.st#63)    /// // "my_future"'s parent. However, if "my_future" is disabled,
[64](https://nexte.st#64)    /// // the spawned task will *not* be in any span.
[65](https://nexte.st#65)    /// tokio::spawn(
[66](https://nexte.st#66)    ///     my_future
[67](https://nexte.st#67)    ///         .instrument(tracing::debug_span!("my_future"))
[68](https://nexte.st#68)    /// );
[69](https://nexte.st#69)    ///
[70](https://nexte.st#70)    /// // Using `Span::or_current` ensures the spawned task is instrumented
[71](https://nexte.st#71)    /// // with the current span, if the new span passed to `instrument` is
[72](https://nexte.st#72)    /// // not enabled. This means that if the "my_future"  span is disabled,
[73](https://nexte.st#73)    /// // the spawned task will still be instrumented with the "outer" span:
[74](https://nexte.st#74)    /// # let my_future = async {};
[75](https://nexte.st#75)    /// tokio::spawn(
[76](https://nexte.st#76)    ///    my_future
[77](https://nexte.st#77)    ///         .instrument(tracing::debug_span!("my_future").or_current())
[78](https://nexte.st#78)    /// );
[79](https://nexte.st#79)    /// ```
[80](https://nexte.st#80)    ///
[81](https://nexte.st#81)    /// [entered]: super::Span::enter()
[82](https://nexte.st#82)    /// [`Span::or_current`]: super::Span::or_current()
[83](https://nexte.st#83)    /// [current span]: super::Span::current()
[84](https://nexte.st#84)    /// [disabled]: super::Span::is_disabled()
[85](https://nexte.st#85)    /// [`Future`]: std::future::Future
[86](https://nexte.st#86)    fn instrument(self, span: Span) -> Instrumented<Self> {
[87](https://nexte.st#87)        Instrumented {
[88](https://nexte.st#88)            inner: ManuallyDrop::new(self),
[89](https://nexte.st#89)            span,
[90](https://nexte.st#90)        }
[91](https://nexte.st#91)    }
[92](https://nexte.st#92)
[93](https://nexte.st#93)    /// Instruments this type with the [current] [`Span`], returning an
[94](https://nexte.st#94)    /// `Instrumented` wrapper.
[95](https://nexte.st#95)    ///
[96](https://nexte.st#96)    /// The attached [`Span`] will be [entered] every time the instrumented
[97](https://nexte.st#97)    /// [`Future`] is polled or [`Drop`]ped.
[98](https://nexte.st#98)    ///
[99](https://nexte.st#99)    /// This can be used to propagate the current span when spawning a new future.
[100](https://nexte.st#100)    ///
[101](https://nexte.st#101)    /// # Examples
[102](https://nexte.st#102)    ///
[103](https://nexte.st#103)    /// ```rust
[104](https://nexte.st#104)    /// use tracing::Instrument;
[105](https://nexte.st#105)    ///
[106](https://nexte.st#106)    /// # mod tokio {
[107](https://nexte.st#107)    /// #     pub(super) fn spawn(_: impl std::future::Future) {}
[108](https://nexte.st#108)    /// # }
[109](https://nexte.st#109)    /// # async fn doc() {
[110](https://nexte.st#110)    /// let span = tracing::info_span!("my_span");
[111](https://nexte.st#111)    /// let _enter = span.enter();
[112](https://nexte.st#112)    ///
[113](https://nexte.st#113)    /// // ...
[114](https://nexte.st#114)    ///
[115](https://nexte.st#115)    /// let future = async {
[116](https://nexte.st#116)    ///     tracing::debug!("this event will occur inside `my_span`");
[117](https://nexte.st#117)    ///     // ...
[118](https://nexte.st#118)    /// };
[119](https://nexte.st#119)    /// tokio::spawn(future.in_current_span());
[120](https://nexte.st#120)    /// # }
[121](https://nexte.st#121)    /// ```
[122](https://nexte.st#122)    ///
[123](https://nexte.st#123)    /// [current]: super::Span::current()
[124](https://nexte.st#124)    /// [entered]: super::Span::enter()
[125](https://nexte.st#125)    /// [`Span`]: crate::Span
[126](https://nexte.st#126)    /// [`Future`]: std::future::Future
[127](https://nexte.st#127)    #[inline]
[128](https://nexte.st#128)    fn in_current_span(self) -> Instrumented<Self> {
[129](https://nexte.st#129)        self.instrument(Span::current())
[130](https://nexte.st#130)    }
[131](https://nexte.st#131)}

[133](https://nexte.st#133)/// Extension trait allowing futures to be instrumented with
[134](https://nexte.st#134)/// a `tracing` [`Subscriber`](crate::Subscriber).
[135](https://nexte.st#135)#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "std")))]
[136](https://nexte.st#136)pub trait WithSubscriber: Sized {
[137](https://nexte.st#137)    /// Attaches the provided [`Subscriber`] to this type, returning a
[138](https://nexte.st#138)    /// [`WithDispatch`] wrapper.
[139](https://nexte.st#139)    ///
[140](https://nexte.st#140)    /// The attached [`Subscriber`] will be set as the [default] when the returned
[141](https://nexte.st#141)    /// [`Future`] is polled.
[142](https://nexte.st#142)    ///
[143](https://nexte.st#143)    /// # Examples
[144](https://nexte.st#144)    ///
[145](https://nexte.st#145)    /// ```
[146](https://nexte.st#146)    /// # use tracing::subscriber::NoSubscriber as MySubscriber;
[147](https://nexte.st#147)    /// # use tracing::subscriber::NoSubscriber as MyOtherSubscriber;
[148](https://nexte.st#148)    /// # async fn docs() {
[149](https://nexte.st#149)    /// use tracing::instrument::WithSubscriber;
[150](https://nexte.st#150)    ///
[151](https://nexte.st#151)    /// // Set the default `Subscriber`
[152](https://nexte.st#152)    /// let _default = tracing::subscriber::set_default(MySubscriber::default());
[153](https://nexte.st#153)    ///
[154](https://nexte.st#154)    /// tracing::info!("this event will be recorded by the default `Subscriber`");
[155](https://nexte.st#155)    ///
[156](https://nexte.st#156)    /// // Create a different `Subscriber` and attach it to a future.
[157](https://nexte.st#157)    /// let other_subscriber = MyOtherSubscriber::default();
[158](https://nexte.st#158)    /// let future = async {
[159](https://nexte.st#159)    ///     tracing::info!("this event will be recorded by the other `Subscriber`");
[160](https://nexte.st#160)    ///     // ...
[161](https://nexte.st#161)    /// };
[162](https://nexte.st#162)    ///
[163](https://nexte.st#163)    /// future
[164](https://nexte.st#164)    ///     // Attach the other `Subscriber` to the future before awaiting it
[165](https://nexte.st#165)    ///     .with_subscriber(other_subscriber)
[166](https://nexte.st#166)    ///     .await;
[167](https://nexte.st#167)    ///
[168](https://nexte.st#168)    /// // Once the future has completed, we return to the default `Subscriber`.
[169](https://nexte.st#169)    /// tracing::info!("this event will be recorded by the default `Subscriber`");
[170](https://nexte.st#170)    /// # }
[171](https://nexte.st#171)    /// ```
[172](https://nexte.st#172)    ///
[173](https://nexte.st#173)    /// [`Subscriber`]: super::Subscriber
[174](https://nexte.st#174)    /// [default]: dispatcher#setting-the-default-subscriber
[175](https://nexte.st#175)    /// [`Future`]: std::future::Future
[176](https://nexte.st#176)    fn with_subscriber<S>(self, subscriber: S) -> WithDispatch<Self>
[177](https://nexte.st#177)    where
[178](https://nexte.st#178)        S: Into<Dispatch>,
[179](https://nexte.st#179)    {
[180](https://nexte.st#180)        WithDispatch {
[181](https://nexte.st#181)            inner: self,
[182](https://nexte.st#182)            dispatcher: subscriber.into(),
[183](https://nexte.st#183)        }
[184](https://nexte.st#184)    }
[185](https://nexte.st#185)
[186](https://nexte.st#186)    /// Attaches the current [default] [`Subscriber`] to this type, returning a
[187](https://nexte.st#187)    /// [`WithDispatch`] wrapper.
[188](https://nexte.st#188)    ///
[189](https://nexte.st#189)    /// The attached `Subscriber` will be set as the [default] when the returned
[190](https://nexte.st#190)    /// [`Future`] is polled.
[191](https://nexte.st#191)    ///
[192](https://nexte.st#192)    /// This can be used to propagate the current dispatcher context when
[193](https://nexte.st#193)    /// spawning a new future that may run on a different thread.
[194](https://nexte.st#194)    ///
[195](https://nexte.st#195)    /// # Examples
[196](https://nexte.st#196)    ///
[197](https://nexte.st#197)    /// ```
[198](https://nexte.st#198)    /// # mod tokio {
[199](https://nexte.st#199)    /// #     pub(super) fn spawn(_: impl std::future::Future) {}
[200](https://nexte.st#200)    /// # }
[201](https://nexte.st#201)    /// # use tracing::subscriber::NoSubscriber as MySubscriber;
[202](https://nexte.st#202)    /// # async fn docs() {
[203](https://nexte.st#203)    /// use tracing::instrument::WithSubscriber;
[204](https://nexte.st#204)    ///
[205](https://nexte.st#205)    /// // Using `set_default` (rather than `set_global_default`) sets the
[206](https://nexte.st#206)    /// // default `Subscriber` for *this* thread only.
[207](https://nexte.st#207)    /// let _default = tracing::subscriber::set_default(MySubscriber::default());
[208](https://nexte.st#208)    ///
[209](https://nexte.st#209)    /// let future = async {
[210](https://nexte.st#210)    ///     // ...
[211](https://nexte.st#211)    /// };
[212](https://nexte.st#212)    ///
[213](https://nexte.st#213)    /// // If a multi-threaded async runtime is in use, this spawned task may
[214](https://nexte.st#214)    /// // run on a different thread, in a different default `Subscriber`'s context.
[215](https://nexte.st#215)    /// tokio::spawn(future);
[216](https://nexte.st#216)    ///
[217](https://nexte.st#217)    /// // However, calling `with_current_subscriber` on the future before
[218](https://nexte.st#218)    /// // spawning it, ensures that the current thread's default `Subscriber` is
[219](https://nexte.st#219)    /// // propagated to the spawned task, regardless of where it executes:
[220](https://nexte.st#220)    /// # let future = async { };
[221](https://nexte.st#221)    /// tokio::spawn(future.with_current_subscriber());
[222](https://nexte.st#222)    /// # }
[223](https://nexte.st#223)    /// ```
[224](https://nexte.st#224)    /// [`Subscriber`]: super::Subscriber
[225](https://nexte.st#225)    /// [default]: dispatcher#setting-the-default-subscriber
[226](https://nexte.st#226)    /// [`Future`]: std::future::Future
[227](https://nexte.st#227)    #[inline]
[228](https://nexte.st#228)    fn with_current_subscriber(self) -> WithDispatch<Self> {
[229](https://nexte.st#229)        WithDispatch {
[230](https://nexte.st#230)            inner: self,
[231](https://nexte.st#231)            dispatcher: dispatcher::get_default(|default| default.clone()),
[232](https://nexte.st#232)        }
[233](https://nexte.st#233)    }

[243](https://nexte.st#243)    /// [`Subscriber`]: crate::Subscriber
[244](https://nexte.st#244)    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]

[254](https://nexte.st#254)pin_project! {
[255](https://nexte.st#255)    /// A [`Future`] that has been instrumented with a `tracing` [`Span`].
[256](https://nexte.st#256)    ///
[257](https://nexte.st#257)    /// This type is returned by the [`Instrument`] extension trait. See that
[258](https://nexte.st#258)    /// trait's documentation for details.
[259](https://nexte.st#259)    ///
[260](https://nexte.st#260)    /// [`Future`]: std::future::Future
[261](https://nexte.st#261)    /// [`Span`]: crate::Span
[262](https://nexte.st#262)    #[project = InstrumentedProj]
[263](https://nexte.st#263)    #[project_ref = InstrumentedProjRef]
[264](https://nexte.st#264)    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[265](https://nexte.st#265)    #[must_use = "futures do nothing unless you `.await` or poll them"]
[266](https://nexte.st#266)    pub struct Instrumented<T> {
[267](https://nexte.st#267)        // `ManuallyDrop` is used here to to enter instrument `Drop` by entering
[268](https://nexte.st#268)        // `Span` and executing `ManuallyDrop::drop`.
[269](https://nexte.st#269)        #[pin]
[270](https://nexte.st#270)        inner: ManuallyDrop<T>,
[271](https://nexte.st#271)        span: Span,
[272](https://nexte.st#272)    }
[273](https://nexte.st#273)
[274](https://nexte.st#274)    impl<T> PinnedDrop for Instrumented<T> {
[275](https://nexte.st#275)        fn drop(this: Pin<&mut Self>) {
[276](https://nexte.st#276)            let this = this.project();
[277](https://nexte.st#277)            let _enter = this.span.enter();
[278](https://nexte.st#278)            // SAFETY: 1. `Pin::get_unchecked_mut()` is safe, because this isn't
[279](https://nexte.st#279)            //             different from wrapping `T` in `Option` and calling
[280](https://nexte.st#280)            //             `Pin::set(&mut this.inner, None)`, except avoiding
[281](https://nexte.st#281)            //             additional memory overhead.
[282](https://nexte.st#282)            //         2. `ManuallyDrop::drop()` is safe, because
[283](https://nexte.st#283)            //            `PinnedDrop::drop()` is guaranteed to be called only
[284](https://nexte.st#284)            //            once.
[285](https://nexte.st#285)            unsafe { ManuallyDrop::drop(this.inner.get_unchecked_mut()) }
[286](https://nexte.st#286)        }
[287](https://nexte.st#287)    }
[288](https://nexte.st#288)}
[289](https://nexte.st#289)
[290](https://nexte.st#290)impl<'a, T> InstrumentedProj<'a, T> {
[291](https://nexte.st#291)    /// Get a mutable reference to the [`Span`] a pinned mutable reference to
[292](https://nexte.st#292)    /// the wrapped type.
[293](https://nexte.st#293)    fn span_and_inner_pin_mut(self) -> (&'a mut Span, Pin<&'a mut T>) {
[294](https://nexte.st#294)        // SAFETY: As long as `ManuallyDrop<T>` does not move, `T` won't move
[295](https://nexte.st#295)        //         and `inner` is valid, because `ManuallyDrop::drop` is called
[296](https://nexte.st#296)        //         only inside `Drop` of the `Instrumented`.
[297](https://nexte.st#297)        let inner = unsafe { self.inner.map_unchecked_mut(|v| &mut **v) };
[298](https://nexte.st#298)        (self.span, inner)
[299](https://nexte.st#299)    }
[300](https://nexte.st#300)}
[301](https://nexte.st#301)
[302](https://nexte.st#302)impl<'a, T> InstrumentedProjRef<'a, T> {
[303](https://nexte.st#303)    /// Get a reference to the [`Span`] a pinned reference to the wrapped type.
[304](https://nexte.st#304)    fn span_and_inner_pin_ref(self) -> (&'a Span, Pin<&'a T>) {
[305](https://nexte.st#305)        // SAFETY: As long as `ManuallyDrop<T>` does not move, `T` won't move
[306](https://nexte.st#306)        //         and `inner` is valid, because `ManuallyDrop::drop` is called
[307](https://nexte.st#307)        //         only inside `Drop` of the `Instrumented`.
[308](https://nexte.st#308)        let inner = unsafe { self.inner.map_unchecked(|v| &**v) };
[309](https://nexte.st#309)        (self.span, inner)
[310](https://nexte.st#310)    }

[315](https://nexte.st#315)impl<T: Future> Future for Instrumented<T> {
[316](https://nexte.st#316)    type Output = T::Output;
[317](https://nexte.st#317)
[318](https://nexte.st#318)    fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
[319](https://nexte.st#319)        let (span, inner) = self.project().span_and_inner_pin_mut();
[320](https://nexte.st#320)        let _enter = span.enter();

[325](https://nexte.st#325)impl<T: Sized> Instrument for T {}
[326](https://nexte.st#326)
[327](https://nexte.st#327)impl<T> Instrumented<T> {
[328](https://nexte.st#328)    /// Borrows the `Span` that this type is instrumented by.
[329](https://nexte.st#329)    pub fn span(&self) -> &Span {
[330](https://nexte.st#330)        &self.span
[331](https://nexte.st#331)    }
[332](https://nexte.st#332)
[333](https://nexte.st#333)    /// Mutably borrows the `Span` that this type is instrumented by.
[334](https://nexte.st#334)    pub fn span_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Span {
[335](https://nexte.st#335)        &mut self.span
[336](https://nexte.st#336)    }
[337](https://nexte.st#337)
[338](https://nexte.st#338)    /// Borrows the wrapped type.
[339](https://nexte.st#339)    pub fn inner(&self) -> &T {
[340](https://nexte.st#340)        &self.inner
[341](https://nexte.st#341)    }
[342](https://nexte.st#342)
[343](https://nexte.st#343)    /// Mutably borrows the wrapped type.
[344](https://nexte.st#344)    pub fn inner_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
[345](https://nexte.st#345)        &mut self.inner
[346](https://nexte.st#346)    }
[347](https://nexte.st#347)
[348](https://nexte.st#348)    /// Get a pinned reference to the wrapped type.
[349](https://nexte.st#349)    pub fn inner_pin_ref(self: Pin<&Self>) -> Pin<&T> {
[350](https://nexte.st#350)        self.project_ref().span_and_inner_pin_ref().1
[351](https://nexte.st#351)    }
[352](https://nexte.st#352)
[353](https://nexte.st#353)    /// Get a pinned mutable reference to the wrapped type.
[354](https://nexte.st#354)    pub fn inner_pin_mut(self: Pin<&mut Self>) -> Pin<&mut T> {
[355](https://nexte.st#355)        self.project().span_and_inner_pin_mut().1
[356](https://nexte.st#356)    }
[357](https://nexte.st#357)
[358](https://nexte.st#358)    /// Consumes the `Instrumented`, returning the wrapped type.
[359](https://nexte.st#359)    ///
[360](https://nexte.st#360)    /// Note that this drops the span.
[361](https://nexte.st#361)    pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
[362](https://nexte.st#362)        // To manually destructure `Instrumented` without `Drop`, we
[363](https://nexte.st#363)        // move it into a ManuallyDrop and use pointers to its fields
[364](https://nexte.st#364)        let this = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[365](https://nexte.st#365)        let span: *const Span = &this.span;
[366](https://nexte.st#366)        let inner: *const ManuallyDrop<T> = &this.inner;
[367](https://nexte.st#367)        // SAFETY: Those pointers are valid for reads, because `Drop` didn't
[368](https://nexte.st#368)        //         run, and properly aligned, because `Instrumented` isn't
[369](https://nexte.st#369)        //         `#[repr(packed)]`.
[370](https://nexte.st#370)        let _span = unsafe { span.read() };
[371](https://nexte.st#371)        let inner = unsafe { inner.read() };
[372](https://nexte.st#372)        ManuallyDrop::into_inner(inner)
[373](https://nexte.st#373)    }

[380](https://nexte.st#380)impl<T: Future> Future for WithDispatch<T> {
[381](https://nexte.st#381)    type Output = T::Output;
[382](https://nexte.st#382)
[383](https://nexte.st#383)    fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
[384](https://nexte.st#384)        let this = self.project();
[385](https://nexte.st#385)        let dispatcher = this.dispatcher;
[386](https://nexte.st#386)        let future = this.inner;
[387](https://nexte.st#387)        let _default = dispatcher::set_default(dispatcher);
[388](https://nexte.st#388)        future.poll(cx)
[389](https://nexte.st#389)    }

[393](https://nexte.st#393)impl<T: Sized> WithSubscriber for T {}
[394](https://nexte.st#394)
[395](https://nexte.st#395)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[396](https://nexte.st#396)#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "std")))]

[Source](https://nexte.st/src/tracing/instrument.rs.html#86-91)

#### fn [instrument](https://nexte.st#method.instrument)(self, span: [Span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html)) -> [Instrumented](https://nexte.st/struct.Instrumented.html)<Self> [ⓘ](https://nexte.st)

Instruments this type with the provided [ Span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html), returning an

`Instrumented` wrapper.The attached [ Span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html) will be

[entered](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.enter)every time the instrumented

[is polled or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.1/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)

`Future`[ped.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.1/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop`[§](https://nexte.st#examples)Examples

Instrumenting a future:

```
use tracing::Instrument;
let my_future = async {
    // ...
};
my_future
    .instrument(tracing::info_span!("my_future"))
    .await
```
The [ Span::or_current](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.or_current) combinator can be used in combination with

`instrument` to ensure that the [current span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.current)is attached to the future if the span passed to

`instrument` is [disabled](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.is_disabled):

```
use tracing::Instrument;
let my_future = async {
    // ...
};
let outer_span = tracing::info_span!("outer").entered();
// If the "my_future" span is enabled, then the spawned task will
// be within both "my_future" *and* "outer", since "outer" is
// "my_future"'s parent. However, if "my_future" is disabled,
// the spawned task will *not* be in any span.
tokio::spawn(
    my_future
        .instrument(tracing::debug_span!("my_future"))
);
// Using `Span::or_current` ensures the spawned task is instrumented
// with the current span, if the new span passed to `instrument` is
// not enabled. This means that if the "my_future"  span is disabled,
// the spawned task will still be instrumented with the "outer" span:
tokio::spawn(
   my_future
        .instrument(tracing::debug_span!("my_future").or_current())
);
```
[Source](https://nexte.st/src/tracing/instrument.rs.html#128-130)#### fn [in_current_span](https://nexte.st#method.in_current_span)(self) -> [Instrumented](https://nexte.st/struct.Instrumented.html)<Self> [ⓘ](https://nexte.st)

[Source](https://nexte.st/src/tracing/instrument.rs.html#128-130)

#### fn [in_current_span](https://nexte.st#method.in_current_span)(self) -> [Instrumented](https://nexte.st/struct.Instrumented.html)<Self> [ⓘ](https://nexte.st)

Instruments this type with the [current](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.current) [ Span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html), returning an

`Instrumented` wrapper.The attached [ Span](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html) will be

[entered](https://nexte.st/struct.Span.html#method.enter)every time the instrumented

[is polled or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.1/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)

`Future`[ped.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.1/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop`This can be used to propagate the current span when spawning a new future.

[§](https://nexte.st#examples-1)Examples

```
use tracing::Instrument;
let span = tracing::info_span!("my_span");
let _enter = span.enter();
// ...
let future = async {
    tracing::debug!("this event will occur inside `my_span`");
    // ...
};
tokio::spawn(future.in_current_span());
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://nexte.st#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.1/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*
